question: Should OpenClaw accept a fail-closed Android math-rendering policy in which an unexpectedly stale WebView provider shows the original LaTeX as a code block instead of restoring the broad JavaScript bridge or file access?
rationale: The patch deliberately trades rendered math for a content-preserving fallback when a required security-narrowing capability is absent; repository policy treats fallback removal and fail-closed routing as compatibility-sensitive product behavior.

options.title: Approve the fail-closed fallback
options.body: Treat the visible original-LaTeX code block as the supported degraded mode and retain the narrowed HTTPS exact-origin message boundary.

options.title: Require a compatible narrow renderer
options.body: Pause merge until Android ownership identifies a security-equivalent rendering path for unsupported WebView providers.

options.title: Retain the prior compatibility path
options.body: Do not merge the Android bridge removal until an upgrade-safe alternative is agreed, accepting that the broader bridge remains temporarily.

recommendation.title: Approve the fail-closed fallback
recommendation.body: Treat the visible original-LaTeX code block as the supported degraded mode and retain the narrowed HTTPS exact-origin message boundary.

likelyOwner.reason: The PR author is assigned and documented the exact Android fallback policy requiring approval.
